answer: A beacon above the knoll records commitments, while correlated equivocation is assessed across the validator set: if k coordinated identities sign incompatible histories, the joint penalty grows as O(k^2), not linearly. Splitting stake among sybils therefore does not dilute exposure; upon detection, their control can incur an exponential multiplier in aggregate capital loss, amplified by asymmetric depreciation of slashed collateral. The tide of apparent identities offers no shelter when evidence links them to one operator.
